answers.value: Confirmed STOLI / fraud-indicator cases and suspected financial anti-selection cases identified during underwriting that require escalation to the SIU / financial-crimes specialist, tracked in the workstation as 'Anti-Selection Escalation'.

Escalation record shows the indicator(s) triggered (third-party ownership, financial mismatch, prior STOLI markers), the evidence, the case number and the specialist recipient; an escalation cannot be submitted without a stated indicator and evidence link.

Escalation follows the approved anti-selection / STOLI referral-trigger matrix v2.1; indicators and thresholds are the current CUO-approved version.

Sensitivity: a single high-severity indicator (confirmed STOLI marker or SDN-list proximity) forces escalation regardless of other factors; multiple low-severity indicators aggregate to the escalation threshold.

Materiality: cases with total insured amount at or above the CUO referral limit ($5M) or with any confirmed fraud indicator are always escalated; below-threshold single soft indicators are documented but not escalated.
Escalation references the anti-fraud / anti-STOLI policy and, where money-laundering indicators exist, the BSA/AML SAR obligation (31 CFR 1025) and the internal SIU referral procedure.
Escalation records and any resulting SAR-referral memo retained 5 years from filing per BSA recordkeeping requirements in OpenText.
Where a SAR is warranted, the SIU files within 30 calendar days of initial detection (60 if no subject identified) per BSA; the underwriting escalation is logged same-day it is confirmed.
All confirmed STOLI / anti-selection escalations raised in the review period (census, ~all flagged cases).
PASS = 100% of triggered cases have an escalation record with a stated indicator, evidence link and acknowledged specialist receipt; FAIL = any confirmed indicator with no escalation on file.

Missed or late escalations are re-raised immediately, the Senior Underwriter is notified, and repeat gaps are reported to the CUO; unresolved after 2 business days escalate to Underwriting Quality / Audit.
Escalations dated within the current underwriting cycle; detections outside the window are handled under the prior-period remediation log.

Applicable rule: anti-STOLI / insurable-interest statutes and BSA/AML SAR filing obligation (31 CFR 1025.320) for suspected money-laundering; internal citation = Anti-Selection & Fraud Referral Policy v2.1 and SIU SAR procedure.
